texts: mixed: the carrying, the threads, Cauldron Hall and the date all come through, and nothing is over-asserted about individual keepers. Two things worth knowing: "day 301 of Year 1" is stored as a plain day number, which the instruction set defines as a day-of-month, so a day-of-year index cannot be told apart from a day-of-month (no wording fixes that); and "the keepers of the Harbor Row" was encoded here as an of-argument while the previous episode encoded the identical phrase as a possession, so the keepers of the two episodes will not answer one and the same question. Putting the possessor in front pins it to one form every time: "On day 301 of Year 1, the Harbor Row keepers carried the silken threads to Cauldron Hall."

mixed: everything is present - Hesper, the threads, the sea-water, the three cauldrons - but the two "in" phrases land as two side-by-side locations of the boiling, so nothing records that the sea-water was in the cauldrons. Stating the containment separately keeps it: "There was sea-water in the three cauldrons. Hesper boiled the silken threads in the sea-water."
good. the forming, the three cauldrons and the "by evening" deadline are all captured, with the mire-essence correctly the thing that comes to be.
good. the storing, Hesper as the agent, and the four clay vessels with their count are all covered.
good. the drawing at sundown reuses the very mire-essence Hesper stored, and "stored" is carried as a property of it rather than dropped.
good. "thirty of the fallen feathers" comes out as a counted subset of the definite fallen-feather set, with the base of the cliff and the morning both recorded.
good. "the feathers" correctly resolves to the thirty she just collected, and the feather bin is recorded as where they went.
good. the bare plural correctly starts a new batch of feathers, distinct from the thirty, taken from the same bin.
good. grinding is treated as changing the feathers themselves, on the same batch Bevin took from the bin.
good. the scattering, the placement around the Stilllight Lantern, sundown, and a rule making each feather of that batch ground are all there.
good. the warding links the ground feathers to the Stilllight Lantern and keeps "against wraiths" as stated.
good. this becomes a fireable strength-zero rule - no wraith of any kind made that approach - with "no" recorded alongside it.
